PRIVILEGED AND CONFIDENTIAL — ATTORNEY WORK PRODUCT
PREPARED FOR THE PROJECT LATTICE DEAL TEAM
TRELLIS BIOWORKS, INC. (SELL-SIDE)

DISCLOSURE RECONCILIATION MEMORANDUM
Disclosed Litigation and IP Matters vs. the Article VIII Indemnity Architecture

Date of preparation: Pre-negotiation session (next session)
Re: SPA Article VIII (Indemnification) — disclosure reconciliation for Schedule 3.14

I. PURPOSE

This memorandum reconciles the matters disclosed on Trellis BioWorks, Inc.'s Disclosure Schedule 3.14 (Litigation and Intellectual Property) against the three indemnity structures on the table for the Project Lattice transaction: (a) the execution draft v4 Article VIII structure; (b) Halberd's second-turn markup as transmitted by Wexler Bright LLP; and (c) the Trellis deal team's approved indemnity positions (the fallback). It states the quantified exposure of each disclosed item, characterizes items without a stated dollar amount, analyzes each item under each structure, states the aggregate quantified exposure of the pending disclosed matters, and flags the item that the approved positions require to be excluded from any special indemnity.

II. THE THREE INDEMNITY STRUCTURES IN REVIEW

A. Execution Draft v4 (Sell-Side Current Draft). Article VIII of the SPA execution draft v4 provides: (i) a true deductible of $400,000 (recovery only of Losses in excess of the Deductible); (ii) an aggregate cap of ten percent (10%) of the Purchase Price ($12,000,000), with Fundamental Representations capped at the Purchase Price; (iii) survival of general representations for eighteen (18) months, six (6) years for Fundamental Representations; and (iv) no special indemnities.

B. Halberd Second-Turn Markup (Wexler Bright LLP, transmitted 30 July 2026). Halberd's markup (i) extends general-representation survival to thirty-six (36) months; (ii) converts the basket to a tipping basket of $250,000 (once aggregate Losses exceed $250,000, Seller liability runs from the first dollar); (iii) raises the cap to twenty-five percent (25%) of the Purchase Price ($30,000,000); and (iv) adds a new Section 8.2(d) special indemnity that covers any and all Losses arising out of or relating to all matters disclosed on Schedule 3.14, is not subject to the Deductible or the cap, survives until the expiration of the applicable statutes of limitation, and (per conforming change to Section 8.5) is recoverable directly from the Sellers without exhausting the Escrow Amount.

C. Trellis Approved Positions (Transaction Committee–approved, 24 July 2026). The approved positions: (i) cap general-representation survival at twenty-four (24) months (36 months is out of policy); (ii) permit a cap up to fifteen percent (15%) of the Purchase Price ($18,000,000) (25% is out of policy); (iii) require the basket to remain a true deductible, not a tipping basket (tipping basket is out of policy at any threshold), with the deductible reducible from $400,000 but not below $300,000; and (iv) permit a special indemnity only if limited to Schedule 3.14 Items 1 and 2 (the pending matters), capped at $2,500,000, with twenty-four (24) months survival, and with resolved matters — including Item 3 — expressly excluded. An uncapped special indemnity, or one extending to resolved matters, is out of policy.

III. DISCLOSED ITEMS, EXPRESSION OF EXPOSURE, AND ANALYSIS UNDER EACH STRUCTURE

-----------------------------------------------------------------------------
Item 1. Trademark Opposition — TTAB Opposition No. 91-284772, Lumenor Devices B.V. v. Trellis BioWorks, Inc. (TRELLIGEN, U.S. App. Serial No. 98/415,882)
Status: Pending (discovery conference held 5 May 2026)
-----------------------------------------------------------------------------

Quantification / Risk Characterization. The schedule does not supply a dollar amount for this item. No damages are claimed in the proceeding. The exposure is characterized qualitatively: the potential refusal of registration of the TRELLIGEN mark and associated rebranding costs of the TRELLIGEN assay line if the opposition succeeds. The Company continues to use the mark at common law. Because no dollar figure is stated, the exposure is unquantified and must be tracked as a contingent cost should rebranding become necessary.

(a) Execution draft v4. As a breach-triggered claim under Section 8.2(a), any Loss arising from loss of the TRELLIGEN registration would be subject to the $400,000 true deductible and would be recoverable only to the extent aggregate indemnifiable Losses exceed $400,000. Any such Loss would count toward the ten percent ($12,000,000) aggregate cap. With no stated dollar amount, the item's contribution to deductible and cap cannot be valued on the schedule alone; the risk is the practical, uninsured cost of rebranding.

(b) Halberd markup. The special indemnity at new Section 8.2(d) would cover all Losses relating to this matter with no deductible and no cap, surviving until the expiration of the applicable statutes of limitation, and recoverable directly from the Sellers. Under the markup, the Company would bear the full rebranding cost, whatever it may prove to be, for an unlimited period — the most adverse treatment to the Sellers across all three structures.

(c) Approved positions fallback. A special indemnity under the approved positions is permissible for this item as one of the two pending matters (Item 1 is within scope), subject to a $2,500,000 aggregate cap across the special indemnity, twenty-four (24) months survival, and coordination with the true deductible structure. Absent a special indemnity, fallback under the general indemnity would apply the approved deductible (between $300,000 and $400,000) and cap (up to $18,000,000).

-----------------------------------------------------------------------------
Item 2. Customer Dispute — Bexley Clinical Partners LLC Demand (Pre-Litigation, Pending)
Status: Pending (demand of 3 April 2026; liability denied 24 April 2026; insurer noticed 28 April 2026; coverage reserved)
-----------------------------------------------------------------------------

Quantification / Risk Characterization. The schedule supplies a stated dollar amount: $1,850,000 in damages claimed by Bexley Clinical Partners LLC for alleged assay lot failures under the 2024 Supply Agreement. The Company has denied liability and asserts the lot conformed to the released specification. Insurance coverage has been noticed and the carrier's position reserved, but no coverage amounts are stated on the schedule. The $1,850,000 represents the face amount of the claim, not a proven liability.

(a) Execution draft v4. The claimed $1,850,000 would be a Loss under Section 8.2(a) only if the claim ripened into a breach indemnity event. Standing alone, $1,850,000 exceeds the $400,000 deductible, so recovery would run on the excess ($1,450,000). The claim is well within the $12,000,000 aggregate cap. Any recovery by the Buyer would be net of the Deductible.

(b) Halberd markup. Under the tipping basket, once aggregate Losses exceed $250,000 the Sellers are liable from the first dollar. The $1,850,000 claim, if sustained, would trigger Seller liability from dollar one (i.e., the first dollar, not merely the excess over $250,000). Additionally, the special indemnity at new Section 8.2(d) would cover this item with no deductible and no cap, directly from the Sellers, and without exhausting the Escrow. This is the most onerous treatment of the $1,850,000 exposure across all three structures, because it eliminates both the basket protection and the cap.

(c) Approved positions fallback. This item is within the permissible scope of a special indemnity (pending matter), subject to the $2,500,000 aggregate cap across special-indemnity claims, twenty-four (24) months survival, and the pending-matter-only limitation. The $1,850,000 claim would fit within a $2,500,000 capped special indemnity. If the special indemnity is not accepted, the fallback general-indemnity treatment would apply the approved deductible (not below $300,000) and the approved cap (not above $18,000,000), with the basket remaining a true deductible.

-----------------------------------------------------------------------------
Item 3. OSHA Citation — Citation No. 1829445 (Region IV), Norcross Facility
Status: Resolved (informal settlement; $46,500 penalty paid in full 17 March 2026; abatement certified 2 March 2026)
-----------------------------------------------------------------------------

Quantification / Risk Characterization. The schedule supplies a stated dollar amount: $46,500, the penally paid in full. The matter is closed. The schedule discloses it as a resolved matter only; no ongoing liability is stated.

(a) Execution draft v4. Because the matter is resolved and the penalty fully paid before Closing, there is no present Loss under Section 8.2, and no indemnity exposure is expected under the v4 structure. Even were the item regarded as disclosable, $46,500 is below the $400,000 deductible and would not be recoverable under Section 8.2(a).

(b) Halberd markup. The markup's special indemnity at new Section 8.2(d) purports to cover any and all Losses relating to all matters disclosed on Schedule 3.14, which on its face includes resolved Item 3. Because the $46,500 was already paid and the matter closed, Buyer could not claim that loss as its own. Nevertheless, the markup's open-ended reference to "all" disclosed matters creates a drafting risk that resolved matters could be swept within the special indemnity's uncapped, undeducted, indefinite-survival coverage. This treatment is inconsistent with the approved positions, which require resolved matters to be expressly excluded.

(c) Approved positions fallback. Item 3 is a resolved matter and must be expressly excluded from any special indemnity under approved position IP-4. The approved positions require that the special indemnity scope be limited to the pending matters (Items 1 and 2) and that resolved matters — including Item 3 — be carved out. Under the fallback, Item 3 contributes no forward liability to the sellers.

IV. AGGREGATE QUANTIFIED EXPOSURE OF PENDING DISCLOSED MATTERS

The pending disclosed matters are Item 1 (trademark opposition) and Item 2 (Bexley customer dispute). Of these, only Item 2 carries a stated dollar amount in the schedule: $1,850,000 in claimed damages. Item 1 carries no stated dollar amount; its exposure is contingent and unquantified (potential loss of the TRELLIGEN registration and associated rebranding costs). The aggregate quantified exposure of the pending disclosed matters is therefore $1,850,000, representing the face amount of the Bexley demand. This figure should be regarded as the floor of the potential special-indemnity claim quantum, since Item 1's rebranding costs are not stated and could add to the total.

V. SPECIAL-INDEMNITY EXCLUSION REQUIRED BY THE APPROVED POSITIONS

The approved positions (IP-4) require that resolved matters — including Schedule 3.14 Item 3, the resolved OSHA citation — be expressly excluded from any special indemnity. Item 3 is closed: the $46,500 penalty was paid in full on 17 March 2026, and abatement was certified on 2 March 2026. The rationale for the exclusion is that an indemnity covering a resolved, fully paid matter would convey to the Buyer an exposure for which no present loss exists and no future loss can arise, transferring value to the Buyer without any corresponding risk to the Sellers. Extending a special indemnity to a resolved matter would also contradict the approved-positions scope limitation to pending matters and would exceed the deal team's delegated authority absent Special Committee approval.

VI. SUMMARY COMPARISON TABLE

Disclosed Item | Quantified Amount | v4 Treatment | Halberd Markup | Approved Fallback
Item 1 (TTAB opposition, pending) | None stated (unquantified; rebranding contingent cost) | Subject to $400,000 deductible; $12,000,000 cap | Full coverage via special indemnity, no deductible/cap, statute-of-limitation survival | Special indemnity permissible (pending matter), $2,500,000 cap, 24-month survival
Item 2 (Bexley dispute, pending) | $1,850,000 claimed | Excess over $400,000 deductible; within $12,000,000 cap | Tipping basket at $250,000 + special indemnity, no cap/deductible, direct recovery from Sellers | Special indemnity permissible (pending matter), $2,500,000 cap, 24-month survival
Item 3 (OSHA citation, resolved) | $46,500 (paid) | No exposure; below deductible | Risk of being swept within special indemnity (undesired) | Must be expressly excluded from special indemnity

VII. CONCLUSION

Of the three pending-or-resolved items on Schedule 3.14, only Item 2 carries a stated dollar amount ($1,850,000), and the aggregate quantified exposure of the pending matters is $1,850,000; Item 1's exposure is unquantified but real (potential TRELLIGEN mark loss and rebranding). The Halberd markup would expose the Sellers to the full, uncapped, undeducted value of these matters via its special indemnity — treatment that is out of policy under the approved positions in multiple respects (36-month survival, tipping basket, 25% cap, uncapped special indemnity extending to resolved matters). The approved fallback caps special-indemnity exposure at $2,500,000 across the two pending matters with 24-month survival, and requires that Item 3 (resolved OSHA) be expressly excluded from any special indemnity, because no present or future indemnifiable loss exists with respect to a fully paid, closed citation, and including it would over-transfer value to Halberd without corresponding risk to the Sellers.

Prepared for the Trellis BioWorks Project Lattice deal team. Privileged and confidential — attorney work product.
